hints: Focus on what colour tells you, purple in hexane always means iodine molecules, $\text{I}_2$, are present in that top layer.
Remember iodine can get into the tube two ways, either it was added at the start and does nothing, or it is made by displacement of iodide by a more reactive halogen.
List which of experiments 1 to 9 end up with $\text{I}_2$ after displacement, then add the ones where $\text{I}_2$ was added and stays unchanged to get the total.
walkthrough:
**Understand what purple means**

Think like a detective. A purple upper layer means $\text{I}_2$ has dissolved in hexane.

Hexane is non-polar and floats on water, so it is the upper layer. Colours in hexane are: $\text{Cl}_2$ very pale green, $\text{Br}_2$ orange, $\text{I}_2$ purple.

**Apply halogen displacement rule**

A more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive halide. Reactivity is:
$$\text{Cl}_2 > \text{Br}_2 > \text{I}_2$$
So $\text{Cl}_2$ displaces $\text{Br}^-$ and $\text{I}^-$, $\text{Br}_2$ displaces only $\text{I}^-$, $\text{I}_2$ displaces nothing.

**Find where iodine is made**

Check the table for iodide being oxidised:
$$\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{I}^- \rightarrow 2\text{Cl}^- + \text{I}_2$$
$$\text{Br}_2 + 2\text{I}^- \rightarrow 2\text{Br}^- + \text{I}_2$$
That is experiment 3 (chlorine + iodide) and experiment 6 (bromine + iodide). Both now contain $\text{I}_2$.

**Find where iodine was there all along**

Iodine solution is added in experiments 7, 8 and 9. Iodine cannot displace chloride or bromide, so no reaction happens.

The $\text{I}_2$ simply stays there. All three tubes therefore still contain $\text{I}_2$.

**Count the purple tubes**

Purple tubes are experiment 3, experiment 6, plus experiments 7, 8, 9.

That is 2 + 3 = 5 test-tubes with a purple upper hexane layer.

options.A: 1 is far too low. It might come from counting only one source of iodine, for example only chlorine displacing iodine, and forgetting both bromine displacing iodine and the three tubes where iodine was added directly.
options.B: 2 counts only the displacement reactions that make iodine, experiments 3 and 6. The trap is forgetting that experiments 7, 8 and 9 already contain $\text{I}_2$ which does not react and also gives a purple hexane layer.
options.C: 3 counts only the tubes where iodine solution was added, experiments 7, 8 and 9. The trap is forgetting that $\text{I}_2$ is also formed as a product in experiments 3 and 6 by displacement of iodide.
options.D: 5 is correct. Iodine is present in experiment 3 ($\text{Cl}_2$ displaces $\text{I}_2$), experiment 6 ($\text{Br}_2$ displaces $\text{I}_2$), and experiments 7, 8, 9 (added $\text{I}_2$ with no reaction). All five give a purple upper hexane layer.
